title: "Check device's route" button opens google.com
finding: The only call to action on the Registration overview page that promises to tell applicants their evaluation route and licence needs links to https://www.google.com. A user who trusts it leaves HSA's site at the moment of the key decision.
recommendation: Point the button at the working requirements checker, or remove it until one exists. Add the page to an automated link check (DSS PR-5).

title: Every link to the "registration and licensing requirements" checker returns 404
finding: The tools page, and result screens in all three self-help tools (51 of 52 risk-class results, 12 of 18 grouping results, 1 of 3 'is it a medical device' results), link to the requirements checker. Both targets return HTTP 404. A link audit of 552 links on 24 HSA web pages found 6 failures, and every one points to this checker. The 404 page offers generic help only.
recommendation: Restore the checker or redirect both old URLs to the nearest working guidance (Registration overview). Replace the generic 404 with a page that names the most likely destinations. Run a scheduled link check across hsa.gov.sg and selfhelp.hsa.gov.sg.

title: Route eligibility conditions are stated differently on different pages
finding: The Registration overview lists 'No prior rejection/withdrawal' as a condition for IBR Condition 2, ECR-1, ECR-2 and EDR. The route guides for IBR (Condition 2), ECR and EDR omit it. Rules on how EU and TGA approvals count (one approval for Class B; not counted if granted via the MRA for Class C/D) appear only in the guides. An applicant who relies on one page can pick a route HSA later rejects, and HSA states fees are then forfeited or not refunded.
recommendation: Hold route conditions in one source and render the overview table and every guide from it. State the EU/TGA counting rules in the overview table.

title: Consequence of choosing the wrong immediate route appears only after the eligibility list
finding: The Class B immediate guide warns that an eligibility error forfeits the registration only at the end of the eligibility section; the Class C immediate guide says fees are non-refundable. The overview table and fees page, where users compare routes, do not mention it.
recommendation: Show the consequence next to the route in the overview table and on the fees page, before the user commits.

title: Unclear whether the Class B mobile-app route is a third condition or an alternative
finding: On the Class B immediate guide, 'Standalone medical mobile applications' appears as a heading after 'Condition 1' and 'Condition 2' with the single line 'It is solely a standalone medical mobile application.' The overview table presents it as a separate immediate route with its own conditions.
recommendation: Label it 'Route for standalone medical mobile applications' and list its full conditions, as the overview table does.

title: Answering "what do I need?" takes 13 pages and 9 interpretive decisions
finding: With the checker unreachable, persona P1 (Class B importer and wholesaler) needs 19 page loads across 13 pages or files, 2 dead ends and 9 points of rule interpretation or arithmetic to assemble licences, route, fees and documents. Licence logic is spread across prose such as 'Licensed importers require a Wholesaler's licence for wholesale supply.' KLM time is 97 s before reading; the pages visited hold 6,841 words.
recommendation: Provide one pre-application summary that combines activity, class and approvals into licences, route, fees, documents and access steps (prototyped in docs/).

title: Payment methods differ between the fees page and the Quick Guide
finding: The fees page says fees are payable via GIRO or eNETS. The April 2026 Quick Guide lists GIRO or online payment by card or PayNow through Stripe, and says cheques are not accepted.
recommendation: Update the fees page to match the current payment options and state what is not accepted.

title: Users must add up fees themselves
finding: The fees table lists a $560 application fee for any Class B, C or D registration on a separate row from each route's evaluation fee, and licence fees in another table. Nothing shows a total for a typical case, so applicants must find and add three or more figures.
recommendation: Show 'application + evaluation = total' per route, and offer a worked example for a common case.

title: Links named after a specific document open a generic index
finding: In the route guides and licence page, links such as 'Letter of Authorisation', 'Declaration of Conformity', 'List of Configurations of medical devices', 'Essential Principles Checklist' and 'Declaration of Conformity to a QMS' all open the Guidance documents index. 'Guide to new application for medical device dealer's licence' opens the SHARE e-service page, where the guidance is a 25.8 MB applicant manual.
recommendation: Link each name directly to its template or the relevant section, with format and size in the link text.

title: Same concepts go by different names
finding: 'Overseas reference regulatory agencies' (Registration overview) and 'independent reference regulatory agencies' (route guides) name the same list. The dealer adverse event form refers to a 'Special Authorisation Route Licence No.' while HSA's pages call these 'Special Access Routes'.
recommendation: Adopt one term per concept across pages and forms.

title: Self-help progress counter overstates the number of questions
finding: 'Is it a medical device' starts with 'Question 1 of 15'. Its decision tree has 12 questions and 3 result screens; the longest path asks 11 questions and the shortest asks 2.
recommendation: Show 'Question n' without a total, or compute the remaining maximum from the current path.

title: Self-help tool shows a US-format date
finding: 'Is it a medical device' shows 'Last Updated: 10/15/2026' (month/day/year), while hsa.gov.sg pages write dates as 'Last updated on 26 March 2026'. Readers using the day/month convention can misread such dates.
recommendation: Use the '15 October 2026' format, and state what the date refers to.

title: Self-help sitemap lists template localhost URLs
finding: selfhelp.hsa.gov.sg/sitemap.xml lists https://localhost:3000/ pages (/, /about, /services, /contact) and none of the tools, so search engines are not told the tools exist.
recommendation: Generate the sitemap from the real routes.

title: IVD Cluster page still speaks of past dates in the future tense
finding: The page says 'With effect from 2 June 2026, HSA will be obsoleting the IVD Cluster grouping' and that the feedback window 'is open until 31 July 2026'. On 15 October 2026 both dates have passed, and the grouping tool says the grouping 'has been removed'.
recommendation: Rewrite in the past tense, or retire the page and redirect to the grouping guidance.

title: Small errors in route guides
finding: The Class C abridged guide lists 'MSDAP' for MDSAP. The Class D expedited guide introduces the QMS list with 'for example' where other guides say 'below', leaving it unclear whether the list is exhaustive.
recommendation: Correct the typo and use the same wording in every guide.

title: Dense evaluation-route table
finding: The overview table packs the EU recognised approvals into one cell of 282 words of Directive and Annex references, alongside nested condition lists. Most applicants need one row.
recommendation: Lead with a short route summary; move the EU certificate list to an expandable section per class.

title: Quick Guide link gives no format or size
finding: Other HSA downloads are labelled like 'Download form [PDF, 297 KB]'. The Quick Guide is linked as 'Quick Guide' via a go.gov.sg short link that opens a 4-page PDF.
recommendation: Label it '[PDF, 4 pages]' and provide the key steps as HTML.

title: Each page shows two different 'last updated' dates
finding: The fees page header says 'Last updated on 26 March 2026' while the site footer on the same page says 'last updated on 15 October 2026'. Every HSA page reviewed carries the same footer date, which appears to be the site build date, next to an older page date. Readers checking whether fees or rules are current cannot tell which date to trust.
recommendation: Keep one date per page, the date the content last changed, and label it 'Content last changed'.

title: Mandatory dealer reports are a Word form sent by email
finding: Dealers download a Word form and email it, keeping the email under 2 MB. There is no online submission, no acknowledgement at submission and no status tracking; the HSA reference number arrives only after the initial report. Device users, by contrast, report through a FormSG e-form. Dealers report under 48-hour to 30-day deadlines.
recommendation: Move the dealer report to a structured online form (FormSG or SHARE) with an immediate acknowledgement and reference number, attachments beyond 2 MB, and a link between initial, follow-up and final reports.

title: "15 minutes" estimate is optimistic and the preparation list is missing
finding: The form says it 'may take you 15 minutes to fill in' and that 'You will need to prepare some information', without listing it. KLM execution time for an initial report with every fact at hand is 12 min 36 s (77 entries, 1,660 keystrokes), before looking up IMDRF codes, GMDN terms, UDI or three years of frequency data.
recommendation: List the information to prepare up front, and base the estimate on observed completion times.

title: IMDRF coding needs a separate website
finding: Section VI asks for IMDRF codes for Annexes A to G and points to imdrf.org; the form offers no look-up, so reporters switch between documents and copy codes by hand.
recommendation: Offer a searchable code picker in an online form, with plain-language terms.

title: Event categories are named differently on the web page and the form
finding: The web page's timeline uses 'Possible death or serious injury if the adverse event were to recur'. The form's AE Category options are Serious Public Health Threat, Death, Serious Deterioration in State of Health and Others; the mapping to 'Others' is explained only in the guidance pages at the end of the form.
recommendation: Use the web page's category names in the form, with the deadline next to each option.

title: Numbering and wording errors in the dealer form
finding: Two sections are numbered 'VII' (Patient information and Healthcare facility information). The field is 'Direct Marking Device Identifier (DM-DI)' but the guidance calls it 'Direct Marketing Device Identifier (DM-DI)'. The guidance says 'a rational needs to be provided'.
recommendation: Correct numbering and wording.

title: Users' form requires a hospital name, even from home users
finding: The FormSG form is titled for 'Healthcare Institutions and Medical Device Users', but 'Healthcare facility name' is a required drop-down of 36 hospitals plus 'Other'. Patients at home and GP clinics must choose 'Other' and type something.
recommendation: Ask 'Where did this happen?' with Home, Clinic and Hospital options first, and show the hospital list only for hospitals.

title: Consent question lets users tick both Yes and No
finding: 'I agree to HSA sharing my name and contact information with the local supplier' is a required checkbox field with two options, 'Yes' and 'No', and no limit on selections, so both can be ticked.
recommendation: Use a Yes/No radio question.

title: Dealers could pick the user e-form from the landing page
finding: On 'Report adverse events', the Medical Devices row of the online submission table offers only the e-form for healthcare institutions and users. The mandatory dealer route is in a separate section further down ('For medical device companies').
recommendation: Add 'Companies: use the dealer form' in the Medical Devices row.

title: Strength: HSA already offers four self-help tools and an AI-assisted classifier
finding: The tools page lists 'Is it a medical device', a risk classification tool, a grouping tool and the requirements checker; the risk classification page also offers an AI-enabled classification tool in beta. The building blocks for self-service exist; the gap is the last link (A-01, A-02).
recommendation: Keep the tools; reconnect the checker.

title: Strength: one current Quick Guide covers licensing and registration
finding: The April 2026 Quick Guide (R9) puts the whole registration and licensing flow on four pages and says both applications can be made at the same time.
recommendation: Reuse its structure as HTML (A-17).

title: Strength: users' e-form keeps typing low
finding: The FormSG e-form lets users submit a photo of the device label instead of typing device details, and shows only the fields that apply.
recommendation: Apply the same pattern to the dealer form (B-01).

title: Strength: clear reporting deadlines
finding: The companies' adverse event page sets out what to report and when (48 hours, 10 or 30 calendar days) in one table, and says when the clock starts.
recommendation: Show the same table inside the dealer form (B-04).
